answer: Amateur-radio call-sign check: each agent links a licensed call sign. Verifiers look it up in the regulator's database, then the holder must transmit a one-time code on air in an assigned slot while public receivers along the river valley and beyond log the signal. Licenses go to individuals who passed an exam, so each extra identity needs another examined operator and station; one call sign maps to one identity, so splitting fails. Limit: it shuts out most people, and borrowed call signs spread like yarrow, so audits and revocation are needed.
